newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian pensioners to protest for higher income.
newsitem.headline: Croatian pensioners to protest for higher income.

text.p: Croatian pensioners, oppressed by low income and plunging living standards, will stage a mass protest in Zagreb next week to demand higher pensions, state news agency HINA reported on Thursday.

The Pensioners Association said protesters would gather in downtown Zagreb on November 23 to demand a 40 percent increase in their monthly income, after numerous appeals to the government yielded no results.

Croatian government, cornered by growing popular demands for higher salaries, has announced this week plans to launch a new social welfare programme in 1997, foreseeing higher expenditures and improved social justice.
It was also due to sign an agreement with trade unions on a wage increase for next year on Thursday.
The welfare law, which has yet to be endorsed by the parliament, envisages social spending of up to 10 billion kuna ($1.86 billion) from this year's 4.6 billion kuna ($860,000).
After a war with its rebel Serb minority the former Yugoslav republic launched an austerity programme in 1993 which has slashed the inflation but impoverished a great deal of its citizens.
